title: Prediction of cell states and key transcription factors of the human cornea through integrated single-cell omics analyses
summary: A corneal single-cell meta-atlas and SVM-based predictor supported identification of candidate corneal cell states and markers, including SLC6A6 in a limbal stem-cell state and TNNC1 in corneal endothelium. Protein-level checks were reported. The study also found that current induced-pluripotent-stem-cell organoid states differ from adult cornea.
ai_technology: The SVM-based cPredictor uses an integrated corneal cell-state meta-atlas to annotate external single-cell data, enabling detection and comparison of rare states and candidate markers.
organization: University of Cambridge; University of Bristol

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The study integrated four human cornea single-cell datasets, used an SVM predictor on external data and reported protein-level marker checks.
evidence.unknown: Candidate marker and cell-state findings require broader independent validation; organoid differences do not establish how to improve organoid models.
evidence.ai_role: The SVM-based cPredictor uses an integrated corneal cell-state meta-atlas to annotate external single-cell data, enabling detection and comparison of rare states and candidate markers.
